title: S&P Global Flash Germany PMI (Sep 2026) — 07:30 UTC / 03:30 ET, the largest single component, printing 30 minutes BEFORE the Eurozone aggregate it is weighted into
source: EST: THREE primaries, all fetched direct 2026-09-09 by this event's own initial research. (1) S&P Global's forward PMI calendar, pmi.spglobal.com/Public/Release/ReleaseDates?language=en (HTTP 200, 23,858 bytes): 'September 23 | 07:30 UTC | S&P Global Flash Germany PMI', inside a same-morning block listed 05:00 India, 07:15 France, 07:30 Germany, 08:00 Eurozone, 08:30 UK, 13:45 US. (2) The publisher's own past-release archive, pmi.spglobal.com/Public/Release/PressReleases?language=en (HTTP 200, 92,883 bytes), records the slot ACTUALLY DELIVERED one month earlier — 'August 21 2026 07:30 UTC | S&P Global Flash Germany PMI' — for both the English and the German-language editions. (3) NEW HERE, and the strongest read: the August release document ITSELF, fetched as a PDF from the archive's own per-release URL (HTTP 200, 132,614 bytes) and text-extracted in-session, states in its own embargo line 'Embargoed until 0930 CEST (0730 UTC) 21 August 2026', with 'Data were collected 10-19 August 2026.' The sibling Eurozone lane logged four per-release archive URLs as HTTP 202 with an empty body; the same host serves them as application/pdf when the request carries a browser User-Agent AND an Accept header that includes application/pdf. 07:30 UTC is 03:30 ET under EDT. Filed estimate on the standing schema gap market-events-data.ts carries — no confirmed-source prefix covers a private PMI compiler, and this lane's hard limits permit a flip only on IR:/BLS:/FED:. The date is not in doubt; the label is about the taxonomy
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THIS EVENT'S OWN INITIAL RESEARCH (2026-09-09), reading the single prior proposal (…from-sp-global-flash-eurozone-pmi-2026-09-23.json) as input per EVENT-RESEARCH.md. TIER HELD AT low ON THE MEASUREMENT THE SIBLING NAMED AS NOT RUN. The proposing Eurozone ledger measured the European block's US-hours footprint and found it absent, then wrote down its own limit: 'A study on cash indices or on EURUSD would be the stronger construction and was NOT run.' Run here, in the print's own 15 minutes and its own market: Yahoo 5-minute bars, range=60d (delivered 2026-06-18..09-09, n=60 sessions), DAX (^GDAXI) / CAC (^FCHI) / Euro Stoxx 50 (^STOXX50E), which are all open from 07:00 UTC. In the German print's OWN window, 07:30-07:45 UTC, the raw DAX ran above its own median on 1 of 3 flash days (p27/p38/p82) and reached p90 on none. THE DISCRIMINATOR: the DAX-minus-CAC residual isolates the German news, because France's own flash broke at 07:15 and is 15 minutes stale by 07:30 — that residual is p38/p62/p37, again 1 of 3 above median and 0 of 3 at p90. The one raw-looking hit dissolves under it: on 2026-08-21 the DAX ran p82 in that window, but the CAC ran p83 and the Euro Stoxx 50 p88 in the same 15 minutes, and the residual is p37 — common European beta, not the German print. SYMMETRIC CONTROL: in France's own 07:15-07:30 window the CAC is quiet (p45/p25/p22) while the DAX is p77/p53/p63; each index is ordinary in its own flash's window. US-hours reproduces the sibling on the German leg alone: EWG-minus-SPY at the US open p28/p25/p68, and EWG-minus-EWQ (Germany vs France) p12/p7/p45, BELOW base rate on all three days. THE NUMBER THE SIBLING RECORDED AS NOT COLLECTED, now collected: Eurostat national accounts (nama_10_a10 / nama_10_a64, B1G, CP_MEUR, fetched direct 2026-09-09) put Germany at 39.6% of the eight-nation PMI manufacturing panel's value added (2025; 40.2% on 2024 data) and 33.9% of the five-nation services panel (2024) — so by 07:30 UTC about 40% of the manufacturing weight and 34% of the services weight behind the 08:00 aggregate is already public, and with France's 07:15 print out, 54.5% and 61.3%. AND THE WEIGHT DOES NOT DELIVER THE AGGREGATE: on the one morning this entry can date from a primary, 2026-08-21, Germany's composite printed 51.0, DOWN from 51.3 and a 2-month low (services 48.5, a fifth straight contraction), while the Eurozone composite 30 minutes later printed 52.1, UP from 52.0 and a 9-month high. The largest component moved opposite the aggregate it is weighted into — the sibling's pre-announcement claim is quantified as a WEIGHT claim and qualified as a SIGNAL claim (n=1, recorded not sized). Publisher-stated flash-to-final gaps show why the aggregate is worth more than its biggest component even though the component prints first: Germany composite 0.0 (absolute 0.4), services -0.1 (absolute 0.6), manufacturing PMI 0.0 (absolute 0.3) on a ~400+400 firm panel, against the Eurozone's 0.1 (absolute 0.3) / -0.1 (absolute 0.3) / 0.0 (absolute 0.2) on ~5,000. NOTHING PROPOSED FROM THE ADJACENCY SWEEP, deliberately and on this document's own evidence: the German finals (2026-10-01 manufacturing and 2026-10-05 services/composite, both 07:55 UTC, from the calendar page and the release's own 'Final August data are published on 1 September for manufacturing and 3 September for services and composite') and German construction PMI (2026-10-06, 07:30 UTC) are dated and recorded in the ledger, but filing three more European prints after measuring that this block leaves no mark even in its own cash index in its own window would add noise on the strength of a null. Full workup and ledger: docs/research/events/sp-global-flash-germany-pmi-2026-09-23.md
